**STEP 1 - Scene:** This is a single whole apple (red-yellow skin, stem cavity visible) sitting on a white plate. It is not a full meal. There is roughly one medium apple's worth of food.

**STEP 2 - Vessel:** A white square plate, about 22 cm across, a side-plate-sized dish. It fills most of the frame. The apple covers only a small central part of the plate.

**STEP 3 - Items:**
- Whole apple (raw, red and yellow skin)
- Faint pinkish smears on the plate, likely apple juice or residue, with no meaningful food mass
- A tiny yellow speck near the lower right of the apple, negligible

**STEP 4 - Volume:**
- Apple diameter: about 125 px out of roughly 350 px plate width, so about 35% of the plate width. At a 22 cm plate, that is about 8 cm.
- Apple covers about 50 cm² of plate area (about 20% of the vessel), but its volume is what matters.
- Apple as a near-sphere: 4/3·π·(4 cm)³ ≈ 268 ml. Apples are not perfect spheres and have a stem cavity, so take about 75% of that: about 200 ml.

**STEP 5 - Grams:** Whole apples have a bulk density close to water, around 0.8 g/ml, since they include air pockets and the stem cavity. 200 ml × 0.8 ≈ 165 g.

**STEP 6 - Energy:** Raw apple is about 52 kcal per 100 g. 165 g × 0.52 ≈ 86 kcal.

**STEP 7 - Sanity check:** A medium-to-large apple weighs about 150–200 g and has about 80–100 kcal, so 165 g and 86 kcal are plausible for what is visible. The smears and speck add essentially no weight.
